canonical_data: rig topology, queue items and their transitions, workflow instances, inbox and outbox entries, chat messages, snapshots, and watchdog jobs in a SQLite database under the operator's home directory
strengths: Work is owned state rather than a terminal list: queue items carry a status machine with closure reasons, handoff and escalation chains, and a guard that rejects completion without a closure reason
Recovery is designed in, with periodic snapshots, restore by name after a reboot, an event log, and a watchdog scheduler whose policies remind or wake a seat when an expected artifact does not appear
It runs entirely on the operator's machine, with no model-vendor dependency and no account, and its daemon dependencies are a short list of ordinary libraries
weaknesses: Its own README describes the product as managing the team the agents form, not the agents, which is how a session manager describes itself; the queue, workflow and watchdog code is what places it above that line
The workflow runtime's header describes the continue step as a read-only inspector in its first version, so automatic advance was not confirmed from the source
Setup writes provider hooks and workspace trust records and edits the tmux configuration, and agents run as the user with no sandbox
It is a single-maintainer project created in April 2026 at pre-1.0 version numbers, supports only the latest published package for security fixes, and has no native Windows support
why_it_matters: Shows what separates a team-of-agents runtime from a tmux wrapper: durable queues with closure obligations, workflow state, and a watchdog, all of it local.
